title: VisionIST box manifest
description: box.yaml - the registry entry for one box. Everything downstream (the index, the README table, the CI build matrix, the webui definition, the fleet generator) is generated from these, so nothing is maintained by hand twice.

name.description: Directory name under boxes/. Lowercase, underscores.

key.description: The config_json section name the service dispatches on. Often but NOT always equal to `name` (the textEmbedding box answers to `sbert`).

version.description: Semantic version of THIS box, bumped independently of every other box and of the fleet.

summary.description: One line for the registry table.

runtime.description: cuda-only means the box refuses to run on CPU; gpu-or-cpu means it prefers CUDA but works without.

repository.description: Image path WITHOUT a registry host, e.g. sipgisr/visionist-clip. The fleet generator prefixes the registry the user picked.

registries.description: Where CI publishes this box. A box present on only one registry is still usable - the fleet generator falls back per box.

approx_size_gb.description: Rough pulled size, so a user can see what a fleet will cost before pulling it.

maintainers.description: Drives CODEOWNERS: these people review changes to this box.

tags.description: Free-form categories. Tags, not directories: a box can carry several, and re-tagging never moves a path.

default.description: Applied when the request names no command.

extra_ports.description: Ports besides the gRPC one (8061) that the box serves, e.g. the HTTP interface of a box that fronts a phone or a browser. Each gets a permanent HOST port from registry/ports.json, issued from the same sequence as box ports, so it can never collide with one. The fleet generator publishes them; the service reads the in-container number from `env` if given, so it can be moved at launch without a rebuild.

name.description: What the port is for: web, metrics. Unique within the box; the key under which the ledger records its host port.

container.description: The port inside the container. Must differ from 8061 and from the box's other extra ports.

protocol.description: What a client speaks on it. Informational: the fleet publishes the port either way.

env.description: Environment variable the service reads for its in-container port (like PORT does for 8061). The fleet generator sets it to `container`.

location.description: Where the box reads the session id from. The fleet's clients need this and it is NOT uniform: yolo and tapnext read the section top level, lightglue reads parameters.

cumulative.description: true when a reply covers every frame the session has seen, not only this call's.

parameters.description: Keys the box reads from the `parameters` object inside its config section.

section_fields.description: Keys the box reads from the TOP of its config section rather than from `parameters`. Rare but real: lang_sam takes `text_prompt` there. A client that puts them in the wrong place gets a silent default, so this has to be declared.

constraints.description: Things a caller gets wrong otherwise: 'needs exactly 2 images', 'images and video are mutually exclusive'.

assets.description: Test fixtures too big for the repo. CI enforces a size cap on committed files; anything larger is fetched from here at test time.

upstream.description: The model or library this box wraps.

security.description: How a fleet should contain this box. The profile is a name, not a list of flags, so the compose settings live in one place (tools/make_fleet.py) rather than being copied into every manifest.

profile.description: untrusted-code marks a box that executes what callers send it. The fleet generator then emits read_only, a tmpfs, cap_drop, no-new-privileges and memory/PID limits for it.

limits.description: Server limits this box recommends. The fleet generator writes them into the compose file as environment variables, and an operator overrides any of them at launch - the image never needs rebuilding to change a limit. Read by contract/serve.py.

max_message_mb.description: Largest Envelope accepted or sent, in MB. 0 means unlimited, which is the pre-limits behaviour and should only be used on a trusted network. Boxes that take a video need more than boxes that take one image.

max_workers.description: Requests handled at once. Omit to keep Python's min(32, cpu_count + 4). A box whose work is a single GPU should be low.

max_concurrent_rpcs.description: In-flight requests before the server refuses rather than queueing without bound. Defaults to four times max_workers.

kind.description: The Value oneof this field is wrapped as.

codec.description: The encoding the box DECLARES in its reply config; a client decodes with it.

when.description: Condition under which the field is present at all.
